Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:30: He said "to you" [lachem] precisely, because her arousal to unification depends on those below, as it is said (Song of Songs 8:13), "O you who dwell in the gardens, the companions hearken to your voice; let me hear it." And he said, "those whose longing is" — meaning, those whose soul yearns for the Shechinah, like a man who pursues his beloved, whose heart burns after her love and does not sleep from his great love for her — so those who have this great longing after the Shechinah give their heart no rest, for out of their great longing and the fire of love for the Shechinah burning in their hearts, when they wake from sleep, sleep and laziness do not overtake them, but rather they arise with alacrity, joy, and love of the Shechinah, to unify her — because through her union with her husband, who is YHVH, they too are bound to YHVH, and their soul rejoices and delights in being bound to the supernal life, in the manner of "let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth," the desire of the lower to be included in the upper, as explained. And this is "MaZKiRim ET" — ET is the Shechinah, YHVH is the Holy One, blessed be He — and "mazkirim" means the language of binding and unification, as in "azkaratah," which is explained as "incense" [ketoret], and ketoret is a binding, for the Targum renders "binding" [kesher] as "ketar."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:31: "Keep not silence" — the reason has already been explained in chapter 4, that she is always singing, in the manner of (Psalms 83:2), "O God, do not be silent," and she depends on those below — therefore it says "keep not silence for yourselves," so that she too will not be silent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:32: It appears worth examining the precise wording of the verse, that it does not say "do not give Him silence" in the imperative form, as it says elsewhere. This matter is precise in the words of Rabbi Abba, the author of the passage: "those whose longing is to make mention of the Holy One, blessed be He, do not give rest," etc. — meaning, those whose established habit is to have their desire and longing set on making mention of the Holy One, blessed be He — this is "who make mention of the Lord" — you are already accustomed to making mention of the Lord, I need not command "do not give silence," for the matter will come of itself, compelled by their great longing, that they should not give Him silence — this is "give no rest," in the manner that one commandment draws another commandment; how much more does their longing to mention the Lord arouse within them that they should not fall silent and their heart not be at rest.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:33: With this, the plain meaning of the verse (Isaiah 62:6) may be understood: "upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen, all day and all night, they shall never be silent" — these are watchmen appointed above by [divine] command not to be silent. But "those who make mention of the Lord" have a wondrous rank, for they need no command, but of themselves, "keep not silence for yourselves." Here is one rectification for the Shechinah, that whoever practices this is surely a great lover of her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:34: Further, among the other rectifications: "when morning comes, they rise early to the synagogue." And it says "rise early" — this too is about love, for out of their great love to be bound to the Shechinah, they run and hasten to the synagogue, as it is said (Berachot, first chapter, 6b), it is a commandment to run to the synagogue, as it is said (Hosea 6:3), "let us know, let us pursue to know the Lord."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:35: It is also possible to say "rise early" in order to be among the first ten, as our sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot, first chapter, ibid.): a person should always rise early to the synagogue so that he merits to be counted among the first ten — as explained, its secret is in parashat Naso (126a), and we shall explain it further on. And so our sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 8a): Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, be early and be late to the synagogue, so that your days may be lengthened.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:36: Especially if he is the first in the synagogue, as the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, parashat Terumah 131a): whoever is first is joined with the Shechinah and stands in the rank of the righteous one, and becomes an object of the King's love; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:37: In the morning prayer we unify the Shechinah and bind her to Chesed — namely, "Abraham instituted the morning prayer" — and after midday, at the time of Minchah, when the sun has already begun to decline, as explained in the Gemara (Yoma 28b), "from the time the walls turn white" — then Gevurah begins to be aroused, as explained at the beginning of parashat Naso (120a) — that is the time of the Minchah prayer, to unify the Shechinah with the left arm, for Isaac instituted the Minchah prayer. And likewise at night is her unification through the central line — Jacob instituted the evening prayer, namely (Genesis 28:11), "and he lodged there, for the sun had set" — for the sun came to her — and so it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Pinchas 224a, and also parashat Vayetze 148a) regarding "and he took from the stones of the place and put them at his head."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:38: And in the Tikkunim (45a), in these words: in the morning prayer, which ascends by the name called "El," the great God, indeed. In the Minchah prayer, it ascends by the name called "Elohim." In the evening prayer, it ascends by the name called YHVH — the secret of the matter is (Psalms 50:1), "El, Elohim, YHVH, spoke and called the earth." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:39: He further says there (45a) that through Netzach, Hod, Yesod one ascends to bind with the three patriarchs, in these words: further, "perfumed with myrrh" (Song of Songs 3:6), "a bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me" (ibid. 1:13) — this is Netzach, which ascends to the right, this being what is written (Psalms 16:11), "pleasures at Your right hand forever [netzach]." "And frankincense" — this is Hod, which ascends to Gevurah [via the left]. "With all the powders of the merchant" — this is Tzaddik [Yesod], which ascends through the central column. — end of quotation. It is thus explained from these passages that the essence of our prayers is always to unify the Shechinah in the aspects mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:40: Further, one must intend every day to unify the Shechinah in the secret of the bed, the table, the chair, and the menorah, as the Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in parashat Terumah (133a), which we shall explain, with God's help, in the matter of prayer. This is an all-encompassing unification for the whole day, and in the Gate of Prayer it shall be explained how in the morning prayer we draw the Shechinah toward us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:41: There are further three things that a person should do every day to draw the Shechinah upon him: first, the donning of tefillin; second, engaging in Torah; and third, giving her food, clothing, and conjugal rights.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:42: Regarding tefillin, it is explained in the Tikkunim (2a) that they are in the Nukva [feminine, i.e., the Shechinah], and one who dons them bears the sign of the covenant and the sign of tefillin, and is a son, and of him it is said, "do not take the mother with the sons," for the Shechinah rests upon them always, in these words: those who guard the sign of the covenant within its boundary, which is eight days, and guard the sign of Shabbat within its boundary, being Yod-Yod Adonai [alluding to the two extra souls of Shabbat] — for their sake the masters of Mishnah have established that a person is never found lacking in either of these two, as it is written, "do not take the mother with the sons" — and those who are not found every day with these two signs, which are the sign of tefillin and the sign of the covenant of circumcision, and on Shabbat, the sign of the covenant and the sign of Shabbat — of them it is written, "you shall surely send away the mother." And should you ask why both must be present in every person every day — it is so that the Shechinah, who is the Yod of Adonai, not be found alone without the Holy One, blessed be He, who is the Yod of YHVH; a person must not be found lacking either of the two, every day. And if not, of him it is said (Proverbs 16:28), "and a talebearer separates close friends" — this one separates the Master of the world from the Shechinah, the female, of whom it is said (Exodus 31:17), "it is a sign forever" — the male being "an everlasting covenant of salt" (Numbers 18:19). Therefore the sign of tefillin is feminine, the sign of the covenant is masculine, and the secret of the matter is (Deuteronomy 30:12), "Who [Mi] shall go up [Ya'aleh] for us [Lanu] to heaven [HaShamaymah]" — the initial letters spell "milah" [circumcision] and the final letters spell YHVH — in the tefillin, feminine, this being what is written (Exodus 13:16), "and it shall be for a sign upon your hand [yadechah]" — a weak/darkened hand ["yad kehah," a wordplay on the unusual spelling]. — end of quotation. In the plain sense of his words there is proof of our intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:43: Regarding engaging in Torah, it is explained in the Zohar (parashat Vayera 115b): Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Yosi were traveling on the road. Rabbi Yehudah said to Rabbi Yosi: open your mouth and engage in Torah, for the Shechinah is found with you — for whenever words of Torah are engaged in, the Shechinah comes and joins — and all the more so on the road, for the Shechinah goes ahead and comes and travels before those people who merit through faith in the Holy One, blessed be He. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:44: So too it says in the Zohar (parashat Bereishit 50a) that Torah scholars who separate from their wives all six weekdays have the Shechinah with them, and they are male and female.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:45: However, in order for the Shechinah to rest upon him, his study must be fixed, not incidental, and so it is explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (238b), in these words: therefore, "when a bird's nest chances before you" — by way of chance, like a guest and lodger who happens by for a moment in his host's house; and there are some whose Mishnah study is a dwelling for the Shechinah, this being what is written (Exodus 31:16), "and the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, le-dorotam [for their generations]" — read "le-dirotam" [for their dwellings], lacking the letters for "dwelling." And there are masters of Mishnah whose Torah is their profession, from whom the Shechinah never departs all their days; but those of whom it says "when a bird's nest chances before you," the Shechinah is with them only by chance — sometimes she rests upon them and is found with them, and sometimes she is not found with them. And the secret of the matter is: sometimes she is found with them, "do not take the mother"; and sometimes she is not found, "you shall surely send away the mother." Chicks are the masters of Mishnah, or eggs are masters of Scripture; regarding those who do not fix their study, "you shall surely send away the mother"; but regarding those who fix their study, "do not take the mother with the sons." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:46: So too it is explained in the Tikkunim (end of 21a): if so, what is meant by "when a bird's nest chances before you"? Rather, at a time when the Shechinah has no fixed place to dwell, she goes about by chance — this is [the meaning of] "whoever fixes a place for his prayer" — as souls act, so the Shechinah dwells with them: a soul fixed in prayer or Torah is a fixed place for the Shechinah to dwell in it; but a soul that has no fixedness in prayer or Torah, but happens upon it only by chance, likewise she dwells with him by chance — this is "when a bird's nest chances before you." So too, a person's soul is called "a bird's nest," and the body is the nest of the soul; and likewise the souls that are her maidens, called "virgins that follow her will," dwell in the bodies that are their nests, by way of chance, at times when they are not fixed in synagogues and study halls — this is "when a bird's nest chances before you." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:47: Regarding food, clothing, and conjugal rights, it is explained in the Tikkunim (22a): further, these ask for sustenance, clothing, and conjugal rights — the time of their union from Sabbath to Sabbath, of which it is said (Exodus 21:10), "her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights he shall not diminish" — and there is none who asks for the sustenance that is her food; and she is the Supernal Mother, of whom it is said (Proverbs 1:8), "and do not forsake the Torah of your mother." "Her clothing" — this is the covering of tzitzit and its wrapping, and the hand-tefillin, of which it is said (Psalms 102:1), "a prayer of the afflicted, when he is faint [ya'atof, wraps himself]." "And her conjugal rights" — this is the reading of the Shema at its proper time. For if these three things are not done for her, for the Shechinah, "then she shall go out free, without payment" [chinam ein kasef] — he has no shame [kisufa] before the Shechinah, he is brazen. Further, "ein kasef" [without payment] — he shall have no shame in the World to Come. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:48: And in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 49, p. 100b), these three things are explained in another manner, which is closer to the subject discussed there: her food, her clothing, and her conjugal rights are expounded in the secret of the three lines [right, left, center], and it says afterward: Rabbi Shimon said, elder, elder, speak your words more openly, for these words of yours are concealed. That elder said to him: "her food" — this is sustenance from the right side, from which all sustenance comes, this being what is written (Psalms 145:16), "You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing" — this is the right hand. "Her clothing" — from the left side, which is the covering of the eyes, from which comes desolation [aveiriyan] to the left, because on the north side, the left, there is defect there, this being what is written (Jeremiah 1:14), "from the north evil shall break forth" — and therefore it is said of Isaac (Genesis 27:1), "and it came to pass, when Isaac was old, that his eyes grew dim from seeing" — and there covering is needed; and of Moses it is said (Exodus 3:6), "and Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look upon God" — therefore tzitzit and tefillin are her covering, this being what is written (Exodus 22:26), "for it alone is his covering [kesuto], it is his garment for his skin" — "for his skin" being through the skin of the tefillin; "his covering" refers to "upon the four corners of your covering with which you cover yourself" (Deuteronomy 22:12). "And her conjugal rights" — from the side of the central column, which is Israel [Tiferet], "Hear O Israel" (Deuteronomy 6:4), and there is her unification — this being what is written (Exodus 21:11), "and if these three things are not done for her, she shall go out free, without payment." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:49: As for what is said, that "her food" is sustenance from the right side, whereas above it was explained that it is Torah from the side of Binah — there is no difficulty at all in this, for sustenance, although it is from the right, is drawn from Binah, for "children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit but on mazal" — and it is explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 10, p. 25b) that this does not depend on "zechut" [merit], which is Chesed, but on "mazal," which is Binah; see there. So too Torah is drawn from Binah, as explained in parashat Kedoshim, and comes to Chesed, and from there is sustenance for the Shechinah, of whom it is said (Proverbs 31:26), "and the Torah of kindness is on her tongue."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:50: Incidentally we have learned that the intent of the covering of tzitzit and tefillin is to conceal the Shechinah, and likewise the soul, from the forces of judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:51: Here is explained the obligation incumbent upon every person to perform and rectify, every day, food, clothing, and conjugal rights for the Shechinah, and through this his own soul is also rectified, for the soul is a part of YHVH, as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:9), "for the portion of YHVH is His people," as we have explained several times; and when the Shechinah is rectified through him, surely she will rest upon him, as it is said (Proverbs 8:17), "I love those who love me" — and so the Rashbi, peace be upon him, also explained regarding the verse "from every man whose heart makes him willing," etc., which we quoted in chapter 4.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:52: These four things we have explained are unifications encompassing each and every day; there are yet several particulars to be explained, with God's help, each in its place. And of one who so rectifies his days in unifying the Shechinah, as explained, it is said (Ecclesiastes 9:9), "see life with the wife whom you love, all the days of your vain life" — as we quoted this passage in the previous chapter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:53: Further, on this greatness, they explained there in the Zohar (parashat Miketz 196b): another interpretation — "in your strength" [Genesis 49:3, regarding Reuben] — this is the "woman" we spoke of, who is strength for one to be strengthened by, in this world and in the World to Come; and a person must merit her in this world so that he be strengthened in that world. Why? Because after a person departs from this world, he has no power to do anything or to say, from now on I will act — for surely there is no deed, reckoning, knowledge, or wisdom in Sheol, where you are going; if a person does not merit in this world, he will not merit afterward in that world — and they established: whoever does not prepare provisions before leaving this world will not eat in that world. And there are good deeds a person performs in this world from which he may eat here, while all of it remains for the World to Come, to be nourished from there. Come and see: Joseph merited in this world and in the World to Come, because he wished to unite with a God-fearing woman, as it is written (Genesis 39:9), "and I would sin against God" — and because of this he merited to rule in this world, and he brought merit to Israel. — end of quotation, as pertains to our subject. It is explained in this passage how great is the rank of one who holds fast to the Shechinah in his deeds, both in this world and in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:54: In general, for all the unifications of the Shechinah that we have explained and shall further explain, with God's help, before performing that unification one must say with his mouth and utter with his lips: this matter or this commandment I am performing in order to unify the Shechinah with the Holy One, blessed be He, and intend the union Yod-Adonai [YaKDoNKY], and intend that through this she will be raised from exile. How so? Going to the synagogue for the morning prayer, he should say: I am going to unify the Shechinah with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the right arm, and intend the intention we explained; and likewise for the other prayers and commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:55: This matter is explained in the Zohar (parashat Tazria, end of 51a), the words of Rabbi Elazar, in these words: Rabbi Elazar said, in all his deeds a person should wish that they all be for the sake of the Holy Name — what is meant by "for the sake of the Holy Name"? To mention the Holy Name with his mouth over everything he does, so that it all be for His service and no other side rest upon it — for He is always ready toward human beings and can rest upon that deed. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:56: Although the surface of his words, saying "over everything he does," refers to worldly deeds that are for His service — for if it is in the performance of the commandments, that is itself the service — nevertheless it is possible that in performing a commandment there may be some ulterior motive, for He who searches hearts knows everything; and when at the beginning of the deed he says with his mouth that it is for His service, for the sake of the Lord, with the intent to unify as explained, he thereby removes any external element that might attach itself to that commandment. And so it appears from his words, saying "in all his deeds a person should wish" — what does "all" include? Surely this means: not only in matters of holiness, which must be mentioned, since the kelipah desires to attach itself to the spirituality of the commandments even more than to material matters that have no substance — but even in worldly matters, he should say "for the sake of the Lord," so that the kelipah not rest upon any of his material deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:57: Indeed, you will find that the custom of the ancients, peace be upon them, was that before performing a commandment they would utter the intention with their mouths, as with Rabbi Abba, peace be upon him, regarding the three Sabbath meals — in the Zohar it is said (parashat Yitro 88a), in these words: Rabbi Abba, when he sat at the Sabbath meal, rejoiced at each and every course, saying, this is the meal of the holy Ancient One [Atika Kadisha], etc.; at another course he would say, this is the meal of the Holy One, blessed be He, and so with all the meals. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:58: He himself likewise said in the Zohar (parashat Tazria 50a), in these words: come and see, it is written, "and all the women whose heart stirred them" — when they did their work, they would say, this is for the Sanctuary, this is for the Tabernacle, this is for the curtain — and so all those craftsmen — because holiness rested upon their hands and that work was sanctified, and when it rose to its place, it rose in holiness. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:59: He further says there, that even in worldly matters one must make mention, in these words: and therefore, whoever builds a building, when he begins to build, must make mention that this is for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He — he builds a building, as it is written (Jeremiah 22:13), "woe to him who builds his house without righteousness" — and then heavenly assistance rests upon him, and the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares holiness for him, and calls peace over him, this being what is written (Job 5:24), "and you shall know that your tent is at peace" — what is meant by "and you shall visit your dwelling" has already been established; but "and you shall visit" means to utter the matter with the mouth when he builds, and then it is written "and you shall not sin." — end of quotation. From this we may infer to all other worldly matters. And so Rav Hamnuna regarding the sukkah, as explained in the Zohar (parashat Emor, end of p. 103); see there — and from this we learn regarding the other commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:60: It seems to me that this is what is meant by (Isaiah 62:6), "you who make mention of the Lord, keep not silence" — that they should verbally mention the unification, "et YHVH" — the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, as we explained above — and thus he fulfills action, speech, and thought, corresponding to the three names YaBaK, as will be explained in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 4.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:61: Of one who rectifies his days with these rectifications mentioned, it is said (Psalms 34:13), "who loves days, to see good" — and this matter is understood through what is explained in the Zohar (parashat Vayechi 224a), that the days which a person rectifies become the garment in which his soul will be clothed, and through the garment of days he merits to gaze upon and delight in the good pleasure hidden away for the righteous, in these words: we have learned, happy are the righteous, whose days are happy, and remain happy for the World to Come; and when they depart, they all join together and become garments of honor to be clothed in, and in that garment they merit to delight in the delight of the World to Come, and in that garment they are destined to be revived and to stand. And all those who have a garment shall stand, this being what is written (Job 38:14), "and they stand up as a garment." Woe to those wicked of the world whose days are lacking due to worldly sins, and nothing remains of them to be covered with when they depart the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:62: We have learned: all those righteous who merited to be clothed in the honor of their days are aroused in that world by crowns with which the patriarchs are crowned, from that river which flows and issues forth into the Garden of Eden, this being what is written (Isaiah 58:11), "and the Lord will guide you continually and satisfy your soul in drought," etc. And those wicked of the world who did not merit to be clothed in the garment of their days, of them it is written (Jeremiah 17:6), "and he shall be like a lonely shrub in the desert, and shall not see when good comes, but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness." — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:63: Here it is said that through the garment of days one delights in the delight of the World to Come, and is crowned from that river which flows and issues forth. With this the verse "who loves days" may be understood — for since the days are garments in which his soul will be clothed, one must love the days, for just as a person loves the garment with which his body is clothed, since without that garment he would be naked, so too, regarding the rectification of his soul, he should love the days, which are garments his soul will be clothed in — this is "to see good" — for through the garment of days he attains to gaze upon and delight in the good of the World to Come, as explained in the passage, and the proof is the reality of the perception the righteous will attain of the light hidden away for the righteous, as it is said (Psalms 27:13), "had I not believed to see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living." And it says "to see," for a person sees only by means of light, and that light hidden away through it is the true vision by which the first man could see from one end of the world to the other, as our sages, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 12a), and elaborated at length in the Zohar (parashat Bereishit 31b) on the ranks of that light.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 9:64: When one contemplates what has been said, he must rectify himself in his Torah and commandments day by day, as the verse says (Deuteronomy 24:15), "on his day you shall give him his wage, and the sun shall not set upon it" — the explanation being that one should give the day itself its own wage, namely its rectification through Torah and commandments, "and the sun shall not set upon it" — for over each and every day there is an appointed angel, as explained in the Zohar (parashat Emor 92a) regarding the reason a dream-fast is required on the very day of the dream, even on Shabbat; see there. Regarding this, a day that has passed without rectification is gone and lost. And for this same reason it says (Avot 2), "repent one day before your death," so that all his days be in repentance, as explained in the Gate of Fear. And if he wishes to say that tomorrow he will rectify and study — we already find something similar in the Gemara (see Eruvin 65b): day-laborers do not borrow by day and repay by night [i.e., debts should not be deferred] — one must not delay repayment but pay off his debt at once, for if he delays repaying day by day, the debt will grow heavy upon him — and Rabbeinu Bachya wrote on this matter in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Reckoning, ch. 11, near the end). And in the Zohar (parashat Ki Tetze 278a) they explained this verse as referring to the prayers that ascend above through Metatron. And happy is he who rectifies his days in the manner stated, for he will surely merit the good hidden away.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:1: Since we were previously engaged in the previous chapter with the matter of the rectifications and adornments of the Shechinah, we thought it fitting to attach this chapter to it, to explain that all the weighty labors a person is obligated to perform for the rectification of the Shechinah must be done with joy, as it is said (Deuteronomy 28:47), "because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and gladness of heart," and it says (Psalms 100:2), "serve the Lord with gladness" — and it is explained in the Zohar (beginning of parashat Vayechi 216b), in these words: Rabbi Yosi said, the Shechinah rests only in a complete place, not in a deficient place, nor a blemished place, nor a sorrowful place, but rather in a place that is fittingly ordered, a place of joy; and therefore, all those years that Joseph was separated from his father and Jacob was sad, the Shechinah did not rest upon him. We have learned, Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Abba: it is written, "serve the Lord with gladness," "come before Him with joyful singing" — to teach that there is no service of the Holy One, blessed be He, except out of joy — for Rabbi Elazar said, the Shechinah does not rest amid sorrow, as it is written (II Kings 3:15), "and now bring me a minstrel," and it was, when the minstrel played," etc. — end of quotation.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:2: I heard in the name of our master Rabbi Isaac Luria Ashkenazi, peace be upon him, that he explained the verse "because you did not serve," etc., "out of the abundance of everything" — meaning, even more so than if you had an abundance of everything. The intent is that one should be more joyful in the joy of the Holy One, blessed be He, and in His commandments and Torah, than in all the wealth of the world — just as it is said of Torah (Proverbs 3:15), "and all your desired things cannot compare to her," so no joy in the world can compare to the joy of a commandment, as explained above in chapter 2 regarding love. And in a similar vein I heard in the name of Rabbeinu Yonah, peace be upon him, on the verse (Proverbs 3:9), "honor the Lord from your wealth" — that he explained it as "more than your wealth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:3: The manner in which a person acquires joy in his heart is when he contemplates the goodness of the Creator, blessed be He, toward him, as we have elaborated at length — whether in the giving of the Torah, etc. — and say in his heart: the Cause of all causes and the Source of all sources, who created and brought into being all existing things for the sake of man, and His particular providence over me — even though His greatness has no end or limit, He watches over a tiny gnat like myself, who am considered as nothing before His greatness, blessed be He, to do good for me with the goods of this world and the goods of the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 10:4: This is like the parable of a king who has countless ministers and dignitaries, and he sees in his province a certain servant, and calls him and says to him: I wish that you serve me and be among the ministers who stand before me, who see the king's face; and he says to him: if you serve me properly, I will place your rank above the honored ministers who are with me. Is it not fitting for that servant to serve his master's service with joy, and say in his heart: since the king, with all his greatness and dominion, lacking nothing at all, has chosen me for my own benefit, that I should serve before him, is it not fitting that I perform my service before him only with joy and gladness of heart?
